statement.p: Consider the function f(t) = 4 \sec ^2(t) - 9 t^ { 2 }. Let F(t) be the antiderivative of f(t) with F(0) = 0. Find F(t).

static.solution:
Ax^n the antiderivative is just the term whose derivative is Ax^n. That is, \frac{A}{n+1}x^{n+1} + C where C is an unknown constant. Also, recall that the antiderivative of the \sec^2 function is the \tan function. Applying these rules term-by-term to our function, we get:
F(t) = 4\tan{t} - \frac{9}{3}t^{3} + C \quad = 4\tan{t} - 3t^{3} + C
Where C is an artibrary constant. We are further told that F(0) = 0 so plugging this into the above general antiderivative, we get:
F(0) = 4\tan{0} - 3(0)^{3} + C = 0
So that the specific antiderivative is: F(t) = 4\tan{t} - 3t^{3}
